segments.source: Equator’s current namesake blend panel names wet-hulled Sumatra, washed Kenya, washed Colombia and washed Guatemala. It lists component regions and several varieties, including Sumatran Onanganjang and Sigararutang, Kenyan SL28/SL34/Ruiru 11 and Colombian Caturra/Castillo. This is unusually useful buying detail, but it is still the current panel of a recurring blend, not a guarantee of every later bag. An older owner post named Brazil instead of Guatemala, illustrating why dated sources must not be merged into one supposed permanent recipe.

segments.source: The direct US listing offered whole bean, several grind choices, and 12 oz, 2 lb and 5 lb. The 12 oz base was $18.50 on October 16. The product image identifies the bag; printed notes and component graphics can lag the current web panel. Check the actual label and roast date.

segments.source: Cedar, apricot, marzipan, milk chocolate and nutmeg are Equator’s current flavor words. Equator’s director of coffee culture describes a medium-dark coffee that can take cream and sugar while remaining drinkable black. This is an attributed roaster judgment, not a Coffeedant tasting. The Kitchn’s older Equator article mentions a household impression of Equator Blend, but its bag predates the current component panel and cannot validate this harvest.

segments.source: The combination is less single-note than a pure chocolate brief. Cedar and apricot might appeal to someone who wants a little lift; they may deter someone seeking only a heavy dark espresso. We cannot infer note intensity or rank it against a different coffee without a shared tasting protocol.

segments.source: Equator publishes 1:15 starts for drip, French press and V60 on the current page, including 24 g coffee to 360 g water for a V60. That is unusually specific for a house blend and lets a filter buyer start with a reproducible recipe. Its espresso-grind selector is not an espresso extraction recipe; a home portafilter needs its own dose, yield and grind.

segments.source: If one person makes drip and another makes a latte, whole beans and an adjustable grinder give more control than pre-ground “espresso” selected at checkout. For a first trial, make the dominant household brew according to the roaster’s method, note the result, then decide if the second method merits a separate dial-in.

segments.source: Equator Blend is a practical one-bag candidate for medium-dark drip and French press, with an unusually detailed current origin panel and Equator’s own cream-and-sugar positioning. The page also offers espresso grind, but gives filter recipes rather than a portafilter target; espresso buyers should be ready to dial in without a roaster shot recipe. Start with the 12 oz whole-bean option and let a saved recipe on the actual bag decide the next order.
